Two auxiliary regular pentagons in icosahedron construction have parallel planes, centers on a common perpendicular axis through sphere center, planes equidistant from center
Pentagonal vertices alternate when projected onto one plane, forming a regular decagon with side x in circle of radius r
i² = r² + x² by 13.10 (pentagon side vs hexagon and decagon sides in same circle of radius r)

Sphere radius to pentagon vertex has components r (horizontal) and h/2 (vertical), giving (D/2)² = r² + (h/2)² and D² = 5r²

(1/5)D² < i² < (3/10)D² — bounds on icosahedron side squared

configuration_map: The proof operates within a sphere of diameter D containing all five regular solids. The key geometric configuration involves: (1) Two parallel regular pentagons from the 13.16 icosahedron construction, each with circumradius r, separated by distance h = r, equidistant from the sphere center, rotated 36 degrees relative to each other; their 10 vertices plus 2 polar vertices form the icosahedron with side i. The decagon side x in the circle of radius r serves as both the 2D decagonal side (for 13.10) and the horizontal component of edges between pentagonal planes (for the 3D Pythagorean theorem). (2) A cube with side c inscribed in the sphere, whose edges serve as diagonals of the dodecahedron's pentagonal faces with side d, related by the golden ratio c/d = phi. All quantities are tracked as squared-length ratios relative to D²: t²=(2/3)D², o²=(1/2)D², c²=(1/3)D², r²=(1/5)D², (1/5)D²<i²<(3/10)D², d²<(1/6)D².
pass_reason: The proof is predominantly algebraic, comparing squared lengths of the five regular solid sides relative to D². Its spatial claims are limited to correctly describing established constructions from 13.13-13.17. The two key geometric descriptions — the icosahedron's two-pentagon construction (Steps 3-4) and the cube/dodecahedron diagonal relationship (Step 5) — are both correctly stated and mutually consistent. The derivation h = r from comparing 13.10 (2D circle relationship) with the 3D Pythagorean theorem is valid. The formula D² = 5r² correctly follows from the pentagonal vertex position. All algebraic bounds and inequality chains in Steps 7-9 are consistent with the established configuration.
